paper_metadata.title: Influence of the Microstructural Texture of Cast Superalloys on their High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour

evidence.quote: The high-temperature oxidation behaviours of Ni base and Co base cast superalloys were studied to determine the effect of different grain sizes and different surface dendritic orientations.

Even if the external Cr 2O3 scales were always mainly lost during cooling after thermogravimetry tests, some parts of this layer remained on the sample surfaces so that it was possible to estimate the chromia thickness.

The depth of internal oxidation (Cr 2O3 and/or CrTaO 4 depending on the alloy) was also assessed and it appeared that there was no differences between the two microstructural finenesses for the same alloy (20µm for all alloys at 1000°C).

For each alloy a sample for oxidation tests, with a coarse microstructure (characterized by a mean spacing between two secondary dendrite arms λ of about 50µm), was cut from the equiaxed zone of the castings.

Elsewhere a part of the latter (about 50g) was remelted in a water-cooled copper crucible in another high induction furnace, in which the alloy solidified with a significantly higher cooling rate. Thus the same alloys were obtained with a finer microstructure ( λ ≅ 25µm).
